description: Guards against the classic failure modes when an agent uses Storywrangler from a SvelteKit app — assuming a dataset instead of discovering the registry, picking the wrong instrument for the user's question, guessing endpoint arguments instead of reading them from the MCP, and mishandling Storywrangler's error surface / sanitized payloads. Remote-function mechanics are the Svelte skill's job, not tested here.

evals.name: start-from-registry
evals.failure_mode: Agent silently defaults to a corpus (e.g. wikimedia ngrams) and starts wiring, instead of discovering what datasets exist and letting the user choose.
evals.prompt: I want to show some Storywrangler data in my SvelteKit app. Set it up.
expected: Does not assume a dataset — lists the registry with the MCP `list-datasets` first
Surfaces the available datasets to the user and asks which one (keeps the user in the loop)
Uses `get-dataset` to inspect the chosen dataset's instruments, columns, and availability before wiring
Defers the remote-function mechanics to the Svelte skills/MCP rather than re-explaining them

evals.name: instrument-fits-the-question
evals.failure_mode: Agent reaches for the heavy allotaxonometer (or the wrong instrument) regardless of what the user is actually trying to show.
evals.prompt: For US Wikipedia, I want to explain what words drove the shift between two specific dates. Which Storywrangler instrument, and wire it.
expected: Recommends the lightweight wordshift / RTD instrument (single date-vs-date shift for one entity), not the full allotaxonometer
Explains the fit: the question is 'what drove the change', not 'compare two systems'
Confirms the entity and the two dates with the user / discovery rather than inventing them
Looks up the instrument's exact arguments via `get-dataset` instead of guessing param names

evals.name: args-and-availability-from-mcp
evals.failure_mode: Agent hardcodes guessed argument names/entity ids/date formats from memory, and skips checking whether the requested date exists.
evals.prompt: Wire an allotaxonometer comparing France and Germany on 2025-01-01 for the wikimedia ngrams dataset.
expected: Reads the dataset's exact arguments (entity id scheme, date format, filter dims, limits) from `get-dataset` — does not guess
Resolves the entities and checks date availability before baking values in (defers to the MCP / storywrangler-analyst)
Maps the instrument's 404 (no data for that date) to a real UI state
Fetches server-side inside the remote function — a public read, no auth invented

evals.name: sanitized-payload-gotcha
evals.failure_mode: Agent treats instrument response fields as plain numbers, so Infinity/NaN values break the chart, and downloads the whole oversized payload.
evals.prompt: My allotaxonometer chart breaks — some divergence values come back as "Infinity" and the response is huge. How do I handle this in my SvelteKit app?
expected: Knows the server sanitizes non-finite numbers — `NaN` → `null`, `±Infinity` → the strings "Infinity"/"-Infinity" — so measure/divergence fields are possibly-string
Handles those string sentinels in the frontend rather than assuming numbers
Bounds the payload with the instrument's limit params, whose names it confirms via `get-dataset`
Does not re-document the endpoint from memory — points at the MCP for the real field/param names
